records.statement: For two independent small samples with binary/discrete outcomes arranged in a 2x2 table, NIST identifies Fisher's exact probability test as an appropriate exact nonparametric procedure.
records.section: 7.3.3 Comparing two proportions, exact test for small samples

records.statement: CDC notes that chi-square works well in larger outbreak-study samples and that Fisher exact may be more appropriate for smaller studies.

Diagnostic test performance can be represented in a 2x2 table against a reference standard, with sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios, and diagnostic odds ratio derived from true/false positive and negative counts.
Sensitivity and specificity trade off as the diagnostic threshold changes; ROC analysis summarizes this threshold-dependent trade-off.
Positive and negative predictive values depend on disease prevalence as well as test sensitivity and specificity.

Structural validity and internal consistency are relevant to reflective measurement models, where items are manifestations of a common underlying construct; factor analysis is not generally relevant to formative models whose items collectively form the construct.
records.section: Assess the relevance of structural validity and internal consistency

records.statement: COSMIN evaluates measurement properties including structural validity, internal consistency, cross-cultural validity/measurement invariance, reliability, measurement error, criterion validity, construct validity, and responsiveness.
records.section: Step 6: Evaluate the nine measurement properties

records.statement: When a competing event can prevent observation of the event of interest, conventional survival analysis can be biased; the source identifies cause-specific hazard and subdistribution hazard approaches as alternatives for competing-risk analysis.
